## 2 | MATERIALS AND METHODS ## 2.1 | Bee sampling We sampled stingless bees in the Valle de Coto Brus, Puntarenas province, southern Costa Rica, in the landscape surrounding the Las Cruces Biological Station (8°47′N, 82°57′W), near the town of San Vito.
Each site was comprised of a 20 × 20 m plot, in which we sampled all bees detected in 15-min netting samples with two field team members actively netting.
We did not sample bees in conditions of high winds, fog or precipitation.
Bees were captured in the order that they were seen (i.e.
rare species were not sampled at the expense of a common species seen first).
This sampling effort was inclusive of all species in the bee community, but we used only the stingless bees from these samples in the analyses presented here.
We sampled foraging bees in the rainy seasons of 2003 and 2004 (June–September) and in the dry season of 2005 (February–May).
Each site was sampled on 10–22 separate days over these periods.
